description_en: The complex of fiveśikharatemples is located in fields in the village of Lamjī, north of Dullu.The monuments are organised around a central temple (001). This setting, often also referred to aspañcāyatanaplan, reflects thesmārtaworship of Hindu gods. No religious activities are taking place at the site. It is possible to suppose that the original religious affiliation of the complex was śaiva oriented. This is inferred by the presence of a finely carvedśivaliṅgaplaced on top of the topāmalakarings of the northeastern monument (005). Thisśivaliṅgawas most probably originally placed inside thesanctumof one of theśikharas. Thesanctumsare all empty.In West Nepalśikharatemples are known asdevala. Thepañcadevalaplan is mostly found in the districts of Dailekh, Achham and Kalikot, which corresponds to the area controlled by the Rāskoṭi kings. This dynasty ruled between the end of the 14th century and the end of the 18th century. This would therefore situate the construction of the Lamjī temples around the 14th-15th century. Nevertheless, Prayag Raj Sharma mentions the family genealogy (vaṃśāvalī) of the Basyautyāl priests from Badalamjī (3 km east of Lamjī) according to which a certain Govinda Acharya, "a contemporary of Jitārimalla", " having failed to surmount the umbrella-ston or āmalaka over these temples, had a Narayan Das Basyautyāl called from Accham for this work. When the work was accomplished Govinda Acarya made donations to Narayana Das and settled him in the village. The Basyautyāl act as the priests of the Acharyas of Bada-Lamjee even today." (Sharma 1972: 22). Sharma therefore suggested that the temple was built at the end of the 13th century, at the time of the Khaśa Malla emperor Jitāri Malla (r. c. 1287-1289 CE). Yet another Jitāri Malla is known to have ruled in Jumla in 1422 CE (see copperplate grant of ŚS 1343 published inPant 2009: 306-307). In the absence of epigraphic records it is therefore possible to date the Lamjī Pañcadevala between the 13th and the 15th century, although an early 15th century datiing seems more likely (Andolfatto 2019: 87-88).The monument is also mentioned inSharma 2012: 103-105.The dimensions of the temples are:-DLK0320-001 (central temple): 515 x 164 x 196 cm- DLK0320-002 (southeastern temple): 321 x 107 x 130 cm- DLK0320-003 (southwestern temple): 290 x 105 x 123 cm- DLK0320-004 (northwestern temple): 310 x 104 x 128 cm- DLK0320-005 (northeastern temple): 305 x 99 x 128 cm
monument_assessment: Slightly damaged (minor damages such as minor cracks, plants, missing stones in plinths)
